items.title: 2.6 Projectile motion (phenki gayi cheez ki motion) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 2.6 with Fig. 2.8, the three boxes and Example 2.5 (PDF 34-37, printed 31-34).

blocks.text: Ab tak hum ne particle (zarre) ki straight line mein motion parhi, yani one dimension mein motion. Ab ek ball dekhein jo kisi height se horizontally (zameen ke parallel, leti hui seedh mein) phenki jaye. Ball aage bhi jati hai aur neeche bhi girti hai, jab tak zameen jaisi kisi cheez se na takraye. Farz karein ball phenkne wale ke haath se point A par nikalti hai (Fig. 2.8 a) aur us waqt us ki velocity bilkul horizontal hai; ise vx kahein. Newton ke first law of motion ke mutabiq horizontal direction mein koi acceleration nahi hoga jab tak horizontal direction mein koi force na lage. Air friction (hawa ki ragar) chhor dein to flight (urne) ke dauran ball par sirf gravity ki force lagti hai, jo neeche ki taraf hai; horizontal force koi nahi. Is liye horizontal velocity nahi badalti aur zameen se takrane tak vx hi rehti hai. Yani horizontal motion aasan hai: ball constant horizontal velocity se chalti hai, aur horizontal distance x yeh hai:

blocks.alt: Ball Y axis par point A se horizontal chalti hai aur curved (mure hue) raste se X axis par C tak girti hai (origin B). A par, do baad ke points par aur C par ek jaisi length ka horizontal arrow vx aur neeche ki taraf arrow vy bana hai jo har baar lamba hota jata hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.8(a): Height se horizontally phenki gayi ball (kitab ki Figure 2.8(a) ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Vertical (oopar-neeche wali) motion bhi mushkil nahi. Gravity ki wajah se ball neeche ki taraf accelerate hoti (tez hoti) hai, yani a = g, bilkul freely falling cheez ki tarah. Shuru mein vertical velocity zero hai, is liye Eq. 2.14 se vertical distance y yeh hai:

Zaroori nahi ke cheez horizontal velocity se hi phenki jaye. Player ki kick ki hui football, cricketer ki phenki ball aur launching pad se fire ki gayi missile, sab horizontal se kisi angle par phenki jati hain; inhen projectiles kehte hain.
Projectile motion woh two-dimensional motion hai jo gravity ke constant acceleration ke under hoti hai.

Aise mein projectile ki motion ko horizontal aur vertical components mein resolve kar ke (tor kar) aasani se samjha ja sakta hai; yeh dono parts ek doosre se independent (alag, ek doosre par asar na dalne wale) hain. Farz karein projectile horizontal se angle θ par velocity vi se phenki gayi (Fig. 2.8 b). vi ke horizontal aur vertical components vi cos θ aur vi sin θ hain. Horizontal acceleration ax = 0 hai, kyun ke air resistance (hawa ki rukawat) chhor di hai aur is direction mein koi aur force nahi; vertical acceleration ay = g hai. Is liye horizontal component vix poori flight mein wahi rehta hai, aur kisi bhi time t par:

blocks.alt: Projectile origin O se velocity vi ke saath X axis se angle theta par nikalti hai aur parabola bana kar wapas X axis par aati hai; raste ke top se axis tak double arrow maximum height h dikhata hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.8(b): Horizontal se angle θ par fire ki gayi projectile (kitab ki Figure 2.8(b) ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Ab vertical motion dekhein. Shuru mein velocity ka vertical component vi sin θ oopar ki taraf hai.
Kisi bhi instant (lamhe) t par vertical component vfy nikalne ke liye projectile ki oopar wali motion ko free fall jaisa samjhein, jis mein ay = -g (oopar positive). Pehli equation of motion se:

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text: Kitab mein do balls ki photo hai jo ek hi time chhori gayin: ek seedhi neeche giri aur doosri horizontally phenki gayi. Har lamhe dono balls ek hi height par hoti hain, yani un ka vertical displacement barabar hota hai. Is se pata chalta hai ke horizontal velocity girne ki speed par koi asar nahi daalti.

Projectile motion mein aksar teen cheezen poochi jati hain: projectile kitni height tak jati hai, hawa mein kitni der rehti hai (time of flight), aur horizontally kitni door girti hai (range). Neeche yeh teenon hain.
Height of the Projectile (projectile ki oonchai)
Maximum height nikalne ke liye yeh equation of motion lagate hain:

Oopar jate hue a = -g hai. Is equation mein initial velocity ki jagah vertical component viy = vi sin θ aata hai, aur final velocity ki jagah vfy = 0, kyun ke sab se oonche point par body ki vertical velocity zero ho jati hai. Aur:
Air resistance (hawa ki rukawat) ho to projectile ki height kam ho jati hai, kyun ke yeh resistance oopar wali velocity ko jaldi ghata deti hai.
Time of Flight (hawa mein rehne ka time)
Body phenkne ki jagah se le kar zameen se takrane ki jagah tak jo time leti hai, use time of flight kehte hain.

Ise nikalne ke liye S = h = 0 lete hain, kyun ke body oopar ja kar wapas usi level par aati hai, yani total vertical distance zero. Agar body velocity vi se horizontal ke saath angle θ par phenka jaye to us ka vertical component vi sin θ hai. To equation of motion yeh banti hai (oopar positive, is liye g negative):
Yeh zameen se phenki gayi projectile ka time of flight hai.
Range of the projectile (projectile ki range)
Projectile horizontal direction mein jo maximum distance tay karti hai, use range kehte hain.
Range R nikalne ke liye velocity ke horizontal component ko poore time of flight se multiply karte hain (kyun ke horizontal velocity constant hai):

blocks.text_alt: or R = vi cos θ × 2vi sin θ / g
or R = (vi²/g) 2 sin θ cos θ

blocks.title: Do You Know ?
blocks.text: 45° se kam angle par projectile ki height bhi kam hoti hai aur range bhi. 45° se zyada angle par height zyada hoti hai lekin range phir kam ho jati hai.

blocks.alt: Ek hi speed se 30, 45 aur 60 degrees par fire ki gayi teen projectiles ki height aur range. 60 degrees wala rasta sab se ooncha, 45 degrees wala sab se door, aur 30 aur 60 degrees wale raste ek hi point par girte hain.
blocks.caption: 30°, 45° aur 60° par fire ki gayi projectiles ke raste (Do You Know; kitab ke graph ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Teenon projectiles ki speed ek hai, sirf angle alag hai. Range R = (vi²/g) sin 2θ: 45° par sin 90° = 1, is liye range sab se zyada. 30° aur 60° ke liye sin 60° aur sin 120° barabar hain, is liye dono ek hi jagah girti hain, lekin 60° wali zyada height tak jati hai (h = vi² sin²θ / 2g) aur hawa mein zyada der rehti hai.
2 sin θ cos θ = sin 2θ hota hai, is liye range velocity of projection (phenkne ki velocity) aur angle of projection (phenkne ke angle) par depend karti hai:
Sab se zyada range ke liye sin 2θ = 1 hona chahiye, yani:
Air resistance projectile ki aage ki motion ko dheema karti hai aur velocity vi kam karti hai; vi kam hone se range bhi kam ho jati hai.

Yeh bhi yaad rahe ke air resistance poori flight mein constant (ek jaisi) nahi rehti. Jaise jaise cheez dheemi hoti hai, us par air resistance bhi kam hoti jati hai. Is liye cheez aahista aahista rukti hai aur girte waqt bhi aahista tez hoti hai. Result: rasta (trajectory) poora parabola nahi rehta balke ek taraf jhuka (skewed) hota hai, aur utarna charhne se zyada seedha (steep) hota hai.

blocks.title: For Your Information
blocks.text: Air friction (hawa ki ragar) ho to high speed (tez) projectile ka rasta parabola wale raste se chhota reh jata hai (pehle zameen par aa jati hai).

blocks.alt: Ek hi launch se do raste: ideal path, yani symmetric (dono taraf barabar) parabola, aur air friction ke saath actual path, jo kam ooncha jata hai, zyada steep (seedha dhalwan) girta hai aur ideal raste se pehle zameen par aata hai.
blocks.caption: High speed projectile ka ideal path aur actual path (For Your Information; kitab ke graph ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Dono raste ek hi speed aur angle se shuru hote hain. Air resistance speed kam karti rehti hai, is liye actual path kam height tak jata hai aur range kam hoti hai. Kitab ka chhota graph actual path ko taqreeban barabar (symmetric) dikhata hai, jab ke kitab ka apna text kehta hai ke yeh rasta jhuka (skewed) hota hai aur utarna charhne se zyada steep; yahan rasta isi tarah banaya gaya hai: choti beech se aage aur utaar zyada seedha.

blocks.title: Example 2.5
blocks.problem: Ek ball 30 m s⁻¹ ki speed se horizontal se 30° oopar ki direction mein phenki jati hai. Woh kitni height tak jati hai, time of flight kitna hai, aur horizontal range kitni hai?
steps: Shuru ke components: vix = vi cos θ = 30 m s⁻¹ × cos 30° = 25.98 m s⁻¹; viy = vi sin θ = 30 m s⁻¹ × sin 30° = 15 m s⁻¹
Time of flight: t = 2vi sin θ / g = (2 × 15 m s⁻¹)/(9.8 m s⁻²) = 3.1 s
Height: h = vi² sin²θ / 2g = (30 m s⁻¹)²(0.5)² / 19.6 m s⁻² = 225/19.6 m = 11.5 m
Range: R = (vi²/g) sin 2θ = (vi²/g) sin 60° = (30 m s⁻¹)² × 0.866 / 9.8 m s⁻² = 779.4/9.8 m
blocks.answer: h = 11.5 m, t = 3.1 s, R = 79.53 m (taqreeban 79.5 m)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne range 89.53 m chhapi hai. Khud calculate karein: (30)² = 900, 900 × 0.866 = 779.4, aur 779.4 / 9.8 = 79.53. Is liye sahi range 79.53 m (taqreeban 79.5 m) hai; kitab mein 7 ki jagah 8 chhap gaya hai.

blocks.caption: Projectile ke formulas
rows: R = (vi²/g) sin 2θ; 45° par sab se zyada

blocks.prompt: Dikhayein ke angle θ aur (90° - θ) par phenki gayi projectile ki range ek jaisi hoti hai. Sab se oonche point tak pohanchne ka time bhi nikalein.
blocks.explanation: R = (vi²/g) sin 2θ. Angle (90° - θ) ke liye sin 2(90° - θ) = sin (180° - 2θ) = sin 2θ, is liye dono angles (jaise 30° aur 60°) ki range barabar hai. Sab se oonche point par vfy = 0, to vfy = vi sin θ - gt se t = vi sin θ / g; yeh time of flight ka aadha hai.

blocks.text: Summary (khulasa)

items: Horizontal throw: x = vx t, y = ½gt²; dono motions ek doosre se independent. Angle θ par projectile: vfx = vi cos θ, vfy = vi sin θ - gt, v = √(vfx² + vfy²), tan φ = vfy/vfx.
h = vi² sin²θ / 2g; t = 2vi sin θ / g; R = (vi²/g) sin 2θ, 45° par sab se zyada; air resistance height aur range kam karti hai aur raste ko jhuka deti hai (utarna zyada steep).
